OUTSIDE NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Visit date: 03/20/2025

Generalized myasthenia gravis. Another stable year. Lid fatigue only at the end of long days; no diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia or dyspnea; no limb weakness.
Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg every 4-6 hours while awake; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol prn. NKDA.
Exam: no ptosis at rest or with upgaze; EOM full; facial, bulbar and neck strength normal; limbs 5/5.
Plan: unchanged. Re-reviewed crisis warning signs, including after respiratory infections. Return in 12 months.

documents.title: Same-Day Sick Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33F with generalized myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine/prednisone, mild intermittent asthma, alpha thal trait; history of parvovirus B19 (2021 stillbirth, 2022 pancytopenia, resolved).
S: About a week ago low-grade fever and malaise, which went away. Since then five days of cough and mildly short of breath. No chest pain. No vomiting or diarrhea. Has used albuterol a few times this week.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.

O: T 37.2 C (99 F), BP 120/78, P 88, RR 20, SpO2 97% RA.
Scattered wheezes both lungs; no rales, no rhonchi. Rest of exam unremarkable.
CXR PA/lat (in office): no pneumonia, no other abnormality.

A/P
Acute bronchitis after a viral illness, with wheeze in a patient with asthma. No pneumonia on film. Albuterol 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for the next several days; continue prednisone and pyridostigmine. Fluids, rest; okay to finish the school week if she feels up to it. Call or message if not improving in a week, sooner for fever, worsening breathing. Follow-up as needed.

documents.title: ICU Admission Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - MEDICAL ICU ADMISSION NOTE
Date: 05/28/2026 20:30

CC: two days of worsening trouble breathing and swallowing after a respiratory infection.
HPI: 33-year-old with generalized myasthenia gravis, seen by her primary care physician earlier today for cough. Over the past two days her breathing and swallowing have steadily worsened. She had a respiratory infection last week and did not seek care for it until today. Brought in this evening.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol prn. NKDA.
PMH: myasthenia gravis, asthma, alpha thalassemia trait; parvovirus B19 2021-2022, resolved.
SH: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: bilateral ptosis; reports diplopia. Nasal speech, drooling. Neck flexion 3/5. Shallow breathing, RR 28.
ABG: pH 7.32, PaCO2 50, PaO2 60, HCO3 24.

Impression: myasthenic crisis precipitated by respiratory infection, with hypercapnic respiratory failure.
Plan: intubation for airway protection and ventilation; hold pyridostigmine while intubated; IVIG 2 g/kg divided over 5 days; continue prednisone 10 mg via tube; avoid drugs that worsen myasthenia; neurology consulted.

Pulmonary & Critical Care

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/28/2026 (via ED to medical ICU)  Discharged 06/05/2026

Principal diagnosis: myasthenic crisis.
Secondary: acute bronchitis (precipitant); asthma; alpha thalassemia trait.

Course: Arrived the evening of 5/28 with bulbar weakness, ptosis, neck flexor weakness and hypercapnia (ABG 7.32/50/60/24). Intubated on arrival. Pyridostigmine held. IVIG 2 g/kg given over five days with neurology. Strength improved steadily; extubated 6/2 without difficulty. Pyridostigmine restarted at home dose; swallow normal before diet advanced. Transferred out of ICU 6/3. Walking independently, speech and swallowing at baseline at discharge.

Discharge medications (unchanged from home): pyridostigmine 60 mg every 4-6 hours while awake; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol 2 puffs prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: outpatient neuromuscular clinic in about 6 weeks; primary care in 1-2 weeks. Return for any swallowing, voice or breathing difficulty.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt - heard from her by message that she was home 6/5 after ICU stay for myasthenic crisis; records requested from the hospital. She is home resting, school year is done for her. Voice normal, eating regular food, no choking, breathing comfortable, cough nearly gone. Taking pyridostigmine and prednisone 10 mg as before, has albuterol. Neuromuscular follow-up 7/14. Offered PCP visit next week - booked 6/16. Knows to call 911 for any breathing or swallowing trouble.

OUTSIDE NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Visit date: 07/14/2026

Seen six weeks after ICU admission for myasthenic crisis triggered by a respiratory infection (intubated, IVIG, extubated 6/2, home 6/5). Since discharge she has steadily regained strength. Now back to her baseline: no ptosis, diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia or shortness of breath.
Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg every 4-6 hours while awake; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol prn. NKDA.
Exam: no ptosis after sustained upgaze; EOM full; speech normal; neck flexion 5/5; limbs 5/5 without fatigability.
Impression: generalized myasthenia gravis, recovered to baseline after crisis.
Plan: same doses. Early care for future respiratory infections. Return in 3 months.

Neuromuscular clinic
